content: The daily dosage of estradiol varies depending on the phase of the menstrual cycle. After menopause, the majority of endogenous estrogen is produced through the conversion of androstenedione, which is secreted by the adrenal cortex, into estrone within peripheral tissues. Consequently, estrone and its sulfate-conjugated form, estrone sulfate, become the most abundant circulating estrogens in postmenopausal women. Structure: Angeliq tablets, designed for oral administration, provide a hormonal regimen that includes drospirenone (DRSP) and estradiol (E2). The molecular formula for drospirenone is C24H30O3, and for estradiol, it is C18H24O2. Each tablet contains 5 mg of DRSP and 1 mg of E2. The excipients in these tablets include lactose monohydrate NF, corn starch NF, pregelatinized starch NF, povidone 25000 USP, magnesium stearate NF, hydroxypropyl methylcellulose USP, macrogol 6000 NF, talc USP, titanium dioxide USP, and red ferric oxide pigment NF. For tablets containing only 5 mg of E2, the excipients are the same, except they include yellow ferric oxide pigment NF instead of red ferric oxide pigment NF. Pharmacodynamics: No clinical pharmacology studies have been conducted specifically for Angeliq. Pharmacokinetics: After administration of Angeliq, serum concentrations of drospirenone (DRSP) reach their peak approximately one hour post-dose. The mean absolute bioavailability of DRSP ranges between 76% and 85%. The elimination half-life of DRSP is approximately 3 to 10 hours. The steady-state concentrations of DRSP are achieved after 10 days of daily dosing with Angeliq.
